# Egami.Video: guide for coding agents

Egami.Video reads, writes, remuxes, trims and edits video and audio in managed code. Frames are Egami rasters, so Egami's
operations and drawing work on them. Containers: MP4 and QuickTime, Matroska and WebM, AVI, IVF, Ogg and the audio files.
Video codecs: AV1, VP9, VP8, FFV1 and Motion JPEG (decode and encode). Audio: PCM, FLAC, Opus, ALAC (decode and encode), Vorbis,
MP3, AC-3 and G.711 (decode). Royalty-free codecs only: H.264 and HEVC decoding are the separate packages Egami.Video.H264 and
Egami.Video.Hevc.

Namespaces: `Egami.Video` (readers, writers, `MediaFile`, `MediaContext`), `Egami.Video.Codecs`, `Egami.Video.Containers`,
`Egami.Video.Editing` (timelines), `Egami.Video.Audio`, with `Egami` and `Egami.Pixels`.

## Egami's vocabulary

Egami has its own names. Use them, not names from other imaging libraries: Egami has no `Image` type, no `Mutate` or `Clone`
and no `Configuration`.

- `Raster` and `Raster<TPixel>` hold an image; `TPixel` is a pixel type such as `Rgba8`, `Rgb8`, `Gray8`, `Bgra8` or `RgbaF32`
  (namespace `Egami.Pixels`). `Raster.Load` returns the type that fits the file; `Raster.Load<Rgba8>` converts while decoding.
- `Raster.Probe` reads a file's size, format and orientation without decoding it.
- `Apply(ops => ...)` changes a raster in place through a chain of operations; `Derive(ops => ...)` returns a new raster.
  `As<TPixel>()` converts to a new raster and `Copy()` duplicates one.
- `Save(path)` picks the writer from the extension; `Save(stream, format, options)` names it. Loading always detects the format
  from the bytes, never from the extension.
- `EgamiContext` holds the settings, `SafetyLimits`, thread count and registered formats a call uses. It is immutable: change
  it with `with`, and pass it to `Load` or `Probe`, or make it the default once at startup with `EgamiContext.SetDefault`.
- Every `Raster` owns pooled pixel memory: dispose it, best with `using`. `Derive`, `As` and `Load` return new rasters that you
  dispose too.

## Entry points

- `MediaFile.Probe(path)`: container, duration, tracks, tags and chapters, without decoding.
- `VideoReader.Open(path)` and `reader.ReadFrames<TPixel>()`: decoded frames as `VideoFrame<TPixel>`, each with a `Raster` and
  a `Timestamp`.
- `VideoWriter.Create(path, VideoWriterOptions)` and `writer.WriteFrame(raster)`: the container from the extension, the codec
  from `Codec` (`VideoCodecs.Av1`, `Vp9`, `Vp8`, `Ffv1`, `MotionJpeg`).
- `MediaFile.Remux` and `MediaFile.Trim`: copy packets into another container, or cut, without decoding what need not be.
- `MediaFile.OpenDemuxer` and `MediaFile.CreateMuxer`: packet by packet.
- `VideoEdit` with `Clip`: joins, transitions, layers and titles, rendered to a file.
- `MediaContext`: like `EgamiContext`, for video; `MediaContext.SetDefault` at startup. The long-running calls take an
  `IProgress<MediaProgress>` and a `CancellationToken`.

## Samples

What a file holds:

```csharp
// What a file holds, without decoding: its container, duration, tracks, tags, chapters and attachments.
MediaInfo info = MediaFile.Probe("metadata.mkv");
Console.WriteLine($"{info.FormatName}, {info.Duration?.ToTimeSpan()}");
foreach (TrackInfo track in info.Tracks)
{
    string details = track switch
    {
        VideoTrackInfo v => $"{v.Width}x{v.Height} {v.BitDepth}-bit {v.ChromaFormat}, {v.FieldOrder}",
        AudioTrackInfo a => $"{a.SampleRate} Hz, {a.Channels} channels",
        _ => "",
    };
    Console.WriteLine($"#{track.Number} {track.Kind} {track.CodecId} {details}");
}

MediaMetadata metadata = info.Metadata;
foreach (ChapterInfo chapter in metadata.Chapters)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{chapter.Start.ToTimeSpan()} {chapter.Title}");
}

foreach (AttachmentInfo attachment in metadata.Attachments)
{
    File.WriteAllBytes(attachment.Name, attachment.Data.ToArray());
}
```

Read every frame:

```csharp
// Every frame as RGB pixels: VP9, VP8, Motion JPEG or raw, from WebM, Matroska, AVI, IVF or YUV4MPEG2.
using VideoReader reader = VideoReader.Open("movie.webm");
Console.WriteLine($"{reader.Track.Width}x{reader.Track.Height} at {reader.Track.FrameRate?.ToDouble()} fps");
foreach (VideoFrame<Rgba8> frame in reader.ReadFrames<Rgba8>())
{
    using (frame)
    {
        frame.Raster.Save($"frame-{frame.Timestamp.ToTimeSpan().TotalMilliseconds:0000}.png");
    }
}
```

Write a clip:

```csharp
// Images into a Motion JPEG clip; the container comes from the extension.
VideoWriterOptions options = new() { Codec = VideoCodecs.MotionJpeg, FrameRate = new Rational(25, 1), Quality = 85 };
using (VideoWriter writer = VideoWriter.Create("duck.mkv", options))
{
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)
    {
        writer.WriteFrame(duck);
    }
}

// Or into a stream, in a format by name.
using MemoryStream avi = new();
using (VideoWriter writer = VideoWriter.Create(avi, "avi", options, leaveOpen: true))
{
    writer.WriteFrame(duck);
}
```

Encode VP9:

```csharp
// VP9 in WebM at constant quality, on the same Quality and Effort scales as VP8.
VideoWriterOptions options = new() { Codec = VideoCodecs.Vp9, FrameRate = new Rational(30, 1), Quality = 70, Effort = 2 };
using (VideoWriter writer = VideoWriter.Create("duck-vp9.webm", options))
{
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)
    {
        using Raster<Rgb8> frame = duck.Derive(ops => ops.Crop(new Rect(i * 4, i * 2, 320, 240)));
        writer.WriteFrame(frame);
    }
}

// Expert settings: two tile columns, adaptive quantization, quantizer limits on VP9's 0 to 255 scale.
VideoWriterOptions tuned = options with
{
    Vp9 = new Vp9EncoderOptions { TileColumns = 2, AdaptiveQuantization = true, MinQuantizer = 20, MaxQuantizer = 200 },
};
```

Remux without decoding:

```csharp
// Copy the packets into another container without decoding; the sound and the tags come along.
long packets = MediaFile.Remux("camera.avi", "camera.mkv");

// Or packet by packet, choosing what goes through.
using IDemuxer demuxer = MediaFile.OpenDemuxer("movie.webm");
using (IMuxer muxer = MediaFile.CreateMuxer("movie.ivf", [demuxer.Info.VideoTrack!]))
{
    while (demuxer.ReadPacket() is { } packet)
    {
        using (packet)
        {
            // Data, the time and whether it starts a keyframe; WebM alpha travels in Additions.
            IReadOnlyList<PacketAddition> additions = packet.Additions;
            muxer.WritePacket(packet);
        }
    }

    muxer.Finish();
}
```

Trim:

```csharp
// Frame-exact: only the frames from 0.3 s up to the next keyframe are encoded again; every other packet is copied.
TrimResult result = MediaFile.Trim("show.webm", "cut.webm", MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.3), MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.8));
Console.WriteLine($"{result.Frames} frames from {result.Start.Seconds:0.000} s, {result.ReencodedFrames} encoded again");
foreach (MediaWarning warning in result.Warnings)
{
    Console.WriteLine(warning.Message);
}

// No decoding at all: the cut starts at the keyframe at or before 0.3 s.
MediaFile.Trim("show.webm", "copy.webm", MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.3), MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.8), TrimMode.Keyframe);
```

Progress:

```csharp
// Reports arrive once the output is open, then at most every 250 ms, then once more with IsFinal set.
// Progress<T> runs the handler on the caller's synchronization context: the UI thread in WinForms, WPF or MAUI.
IProgress<MediaProgress> progress = new Progress<MediaProgress>(p =>
    Console.Write($"\r{p.Position.ToTimeSpan():c} {p.Fraction ?? 0:P0} {p.Frames} frames {p.Speed:0.0}x"));
long packets = MediaFile.Remux("camera.avi", "camera.mkv", progress: progress);
```

Join clips:

```csharp
// Three clips of different sizes and rates, fitted to one 320x180 canvas at 25 fps, with fades at both ends.
VideoEdit edit = new(new EditCanvas(320, 180, new Rational(25, 1)) { Fit = ClipFit.Contain });
edit.Track
    .Add(Clip.Open("intro.avi").FadeIn(MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.5)))
    .Add(Clip.Open("talk.avi").Trim(MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.5), MediaTime.FromSeconds(1.5)))
    .Add(Clip.Open("outro.avi").FadeOut(MediaTime.FromSeconds(0.5)));
EditPlan plan = edit.Render("joined.mkv", new EditRenderOptions { Writer = new VideoWriterOptions { Codec = MotionJpegCodec.Instance, Quality = 80 } });
Console.WriteLine($"{plan.FrameCount} frames, {plan.Duration.Seconds} s");
```

## Common mistakes

- Not disposing frames. Each `VideoFrame` owns a raster from the pool: dispose it in the loop, as the samples do.
- Decoding and encoding again to change the container. `MediaFile.Remux` copies the packets, keeps the sound and loses no
  quality.
- Expecting H.264 (most MP4 files) or HEVC to decode with this package alone. Add Egami.Video.H264 or Egami.Video.Hevc and call
  `WithH264()` or `WithHevc()` on the `MediaContext`; without them their packets are only copied through.
- Expecting an H.264 or HEVC encoder. There is none; encode AV1, VP9 or VP8 for delivery and FFV1 for lossless archives.
- Converting every frame to RGB when YUV is enough. `reader.ReadFrames()` without a pixel type gives the decoder's planar YUV
  frames, with no conversion.
- Trimming at keyframes when frame accuracy matters: the default `MediaFile.Trim` mode is frame-exact; `TrimMode.Keyframe`
  only copies.
